paragraphs.p2: Final owner-approval candidate • Contract revision 1.0 • 11 October 2026
paragraphs.p3: STATUS: OWNER REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is a proposed contract, not an approval to implement, call external AI, publish, or certify any supplier output.
paragraphs.p5: Business scope: include PET_PORTRAIT, WATERCOLOR, LINE_ART, VINTAGE_PORTRAIT and AI_TRANSFORM in the final software architecture. “Included” does not mean activated in production. Vintage has no reported Master 500 assignments and should be implemented as disabled capability unless the owner explicitly approves a launch use case.
paragraphs.p6: Recommended cost policy: deterministic-first preprocessing, caching of exact accepted bytes, bounded retries, fixed provider/model allowlists, per-shop budgets and manual review for identity/style fidelity. These are recommendations requiring owner approval, not requirements explicitly fixed by Blueprint v6.0.
paragraphs.p8: Blueprint v6.0 §8: versioned prompts, provenance, cost telemetry and human escalation; AI never creates execution authority.
paragraphs.p9: Blueprint v6.0 §§12–14 and §13.2: named engines, approved personalization, immutable template/version lineage, print geometry, same approved payload for preview and production.
paragraphs.p10: Blueprint v6.0 §13.3–13.4: explicit promotion approval and supplier-specific authoritative geometry.
paragraphs.p11: Master 500 v2 contains 500 product entries. Codex reports engine counts PET_PORTRAIT 79, WATERCOLOR 83, LINE_ART 43, VINTAGE_PORTRAIT 0, AI_TRANSFORM 11. Reconcile these with the committed migration inventory before treating counts as certified.
paragraphs.p12: Source documents do NOT specify model weights, artistic algorithm, visual pass thresholds, provider costs, licensed fixture files or consent wording. The parameters below are PROPOSED, not source-approved.
paragraphs.p17: Authorized shop, product, order/design context; engine_id and semantic contract version; approved source asset hash and rights record; approved personalization; template/provider/variant and geometry version; requested output mode.
paragraphs.p19: Immutable accepted bytes + SHA-256, MIME, dimensions, color profile where known, engine/model/prompt/config versions, template version, source hash, job idempotency key, QA evidence, reviewer decision and charge provenance.
paragraphs.p21: Exact accepted bytes reproduced from storage; never regenerate generative outputs to claim byte equality. Deterministic preprocessing may be recomputed and hashed.
paragraphs.p23: Shop-scoped capabilities and nonce/CSRF where applicable; never cross-shop reads; server-side allowlists; reject untrusted remote fetch and metadata-driven command execution.
paragraphs.p25: DRAFT → INPUT_VERIFIED → GENERATED → TECHNICAL_QA → HUMAN_REVIEW → APPROVED or REJECTED. Production readiness only from APPROVED with matching frozen template/payload hashes.
paragraphs.p27: Missing rights/consent, invalid image, unsupported format/model, budget exhaustion, failed QA or stale approval → fail closed with actionable error and audit record.
paragraphs.p29: Proposed: per-job max input bytes, decoded pixels, execution time, generated variants, retries and cost; concrete numbers must be set against deployed host/provider limits and approved budgets.
paragraphs.p31: Minimize retention of personal photos; encrypt/protect originals; explicit retention/deletion policy; no sensitive asset URLs in logs; preserve audit hashes without exposing image content.
paragraphs.p35: PROPOSED PRODUCT BEHAVIOR: Pet photo → stylized portrait preserving species, coat pattern, eye/ear placement and distinguishing marks. No added animals, collars or text unless explicitly selected.
paragraphs.p36: OWNER DECISION: Owner choose 1–2 named launch styles, single vs multiple pets, crop/background, accessories and how to handle occluded faces.
paragraphs.p37: ACCEPTANCE: Human side-by-side source/result identity checklist; reject changed coat marks, wrong pet count, distorted anatomy, missing requested features.
paragraphs.p38: IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY: Versioned adapter; no supplier call or production enablement without separate authorization. Missing style reference or fixture means NOT CERTIFIED.
paragraphs.p40: PROPOSED PRODUCT BEHAVIOR: Approved image → watercolor aesthetic with softened edges, visible pigment texture and retained primary composition; no uncontrolled color/subject drift.
paragraphs.p41: OWNER DECISION: Owner choose palette, background transparency/paper texture, subject types and how much simplification is acceptable.
paragraphs.p42: ACCEPTANCE: Reference-guided review for subject recognizability, color stability and template bleed; reject muddy faces and illegible personalization.
paragraphs.p43: IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY: Versioned adapter; no supplier call or production enablement without separate authorization. Missing style reference or fixture means NOT CERTIFIED.
paragraphs.p45: PROPOSED PRODUCT BEHAVIOR: Approved image → clean contour artwork with simplified shapes, printable stroke width and optional monochrome background. Deterministic vector tracing preferred only when it meets approved style.
paragraphs.p46: OWNER DECISION: Owner select minimalist vs detailed, one-color vs two-color, subject classes, background removal and per-provider minimum stroke width.
paragraphs.p47: ACCEPTANCE: Machine checks for stroke width/contrast/transparent pixels where applicable; human checks for missing distinguishing features and visual clutter.
paragraphs.p48: IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY: Versioned adapter; no supplier call or production enablement without separate authorization. Missing style reference or fixture means NOT CERTIFIED.
paragraphs.p50: PROPOSED PRODUCT BEHAVIOR: Optional future capability: modern image → clearly stylized vintage-inspired illustration. Never present as authentic historic photo or claim real historical identity. Disabled for catalog launch unless assigned approved product.
paragraphs.p51: OWNER DECISION: Owner decide required launch status, era/style reference, permitted wardrobe/background substitutions, disclosure and face-fidelity policy.
paragraphs.p52: ACCEPTANCE: Era-consistency reference rubric; no deceptive historical claims, no unauthorized real-person likeness changes, reject obvious identity drift.
paragraphs.p53: IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY: Versioned adapter; no supplier call or production enablement without separate authorization. Missing style reference or fixture means NOT CERTIFIED.
paragraphs.p55: PROPOSED PRODUCT BEHAVIOR: Controlled transformation dispatcher limited to owner-approved named modes; each mode has its own prompt/schema/version and acceptance fixture. No unrestricted buyer prompt passed directly to a model.
paragraphs.p56: OWNER DECISION: Owner enumerate allowed modes (e.g. illustrative style variants), input variables, identity preservation, forbidden changes, fallback and review policy.
paragraphs.p57: ACCEPTANCE: Per-mode fixtures and adversarial prompt-injection tests; reviewer checks identity/style; unsupported mode rejected rather than generic best-effort output.
paragraphs.p58: IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY: Versioned adapter; no supplier call or production enablement without separate authorization. Missing style reference or fixture means NOT CERTIFIED.
paragraphs.p59: 4. Commercial quality and print QA gates
paragraphs.p60: Input: decode entire image, verify orientation, alpha, color profile, bounds and unsupported formats; do not rely on header-only validation.
paragraphs.p61: Artwork: compare source/result composition and approved rubric; require operator sign-off for subject likeness and commercial appeal.
paragraphs.p62: Production: validate output DPI against exact print size and provider template, safe zones, bleed, panel seams, transparency and minimum text/stroke size. No universal DPI or bleed threshold without a supplier template.
paragraphs.p63: Consistency: preview and production artifact must derive from the same frozen approved payload; reject stale template or changed image hash.
paragraphs.p64: Etsy readiness: listing images must not misrepresent product appearance; provide mockup disclaimers where needed; verify image and personalization rights before publication.
paragraphs.p65: Sampling: include at least one positive, boundary and negative fixture for each approved engine/mode and each materially different template class; additional human-rated reference sets for subjective style.
paragraphs.p70: Try deterministic transform only if approved output quality meets engine rubric; otherwise route to an allowlisted AI provider/model.
paragraphs.p72: Content-addressed cache keyed by authorized shop scope + source hash + engine/prompt/model/config + approved template version; never share private image outputs across shops.
paragraphs.p74: Generate one candidate initially; human-approved additional candidate only when justified. Never infinite regeneration.
paragraphs.p76: Require owner-set maximum spend per job, per shop/day and per engine/month, with atomic reservation and reconciled actual charges.
paragraphs.p78: Bound retry count and distinguish transient transport failure from quality rejection. Idempotency prevents double billing where supported.
paragraphs.p80: Unsupported provider/engine, exhausted budget or QA failure → pending review; never silently substitute another style/model.
paragraphs.p82: Track median/95th-percentile latency, cost per approved artifact, first-pass approval, rejection reason, retry count and human review time; no personal image data in metrics.
paragraphs.p84: 6. Fixture and licensing manifest — owner to supply
paragraphs.p85: No licensed fixture bytes or permission records are included in this package. Synthetic images can validate plumbing but CANNOT certify likeness, style quality or commercial rights.
paragraphs.p90: Owner-approved input + expected/reference output, source/result hashes, dimensions, engine mode and signed visual rubric
paragraphs.p93: Failure/rejection example: identity drift, unsupported image, wrong shop or invalid template
paragraphs.p96: Boundary example: small source, transparency, multiple subjects or print edge as relevant
paragraphs.p99: Rights holder, license/permission grant, commercial/derivative/AI-processing scope, expiration and allowed storage
paragraphs.p102: If identifiable people or private photographs: consent/authorization evidence and retention terms
paragraphs.p105: Exact supplier template/version and approved print specs for representative product/variant
paragraphs.p108: Manifest fields: fixture_id, engine_id, mode, version, source_asset_sha256, result_asset_sha256, MIME, pixel_size, provenance, license_holder, license_uri_or_document, permitted_uses, consent_basis, review_owner, approved_at, expiry, QA rubric revision, template_id, supplier_route, storage_location. Do not put secrets or raw personal photos in public GitHub fixtures.
paragraphs.p110: Contract tests: typed schema, invalid options, stale contract versions, hash/idempotency, shop scope, capability/nonce and audit.
paragraphs.p111: Artifact tests: decoded pixels, alpha/profile handling, print geometry, output hash, safe-zone/bleed, font and PDF compatibility; verify immutable stored bytes.
paragraphs.p112: AI integration: stub providers with deterministic fixtures, request budget accounting, retry/failure paths, cancellation, replay and explicit human review. No live provider calls under STOP ALL.
paragraphs.p113: Visual tests: human-approved reference pairs; record reviewer and pass/fail reasons. Do not infer subjective artistic quality from byte equality.
paragraphs.p114: Lifecycle tests: source → generation → technical QA → approval → listing/order binding → readiness; reject changed source, template or review evidence.
paragraphs.p115: Release gate: complete fixture/rights manifest, owner-approved contract revision, exact-head audit, external supplier certification and separate human release authorization.
paragraphs.p121: All five engines in software; VINTAGE disabled until first approved catalog use
paragraphs.p124: One named style; single pet first; multi-pet gated
paragraphs.p133: Choose one named era; label as stylized; no live listing
paragraphs.p136: No arbitrary modes; approve a finite mode registry
paragraphs.p142: Owner supplies monetary ceilings and allowed retry count
paragraphs.p145: Owner supplies documented policy and licensed fixture evidence
paragraphs.p148: Owner provides reference pairs and signs QA rubric
